chapter: Los Angeles: Chico Hamilton, Webster, Giuffre
title: A forward-thinking approach: tuning the guitar randomly
summary: He explains his low boredom threshold and exercise of retuning his guitar at random, as with Gary Larson.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Before we get to New York and John, you also came across Brookmeyer and Jim Giuffre and (this was?)…
…happening out on the West Coast at first, right?
Because I’m thinking about your forward-thinking approach, which is not new. You seem to have been a forward thinker way back in the beginning.
I have a low boredom threshold, that’s part of it, I guess. (laughs)

In fact, what I, what I did… I tuned… a lot of that… I used to do that with Gary Larson, the Far Side guy, who was… He would come… I told you, with, with his imagination and everything, his guitar-playing was very middle-of-the-road. So I’d take his guitar and tune it randomly, and I’d say, “Okay, Gary, make something outta this.” Didn’t I tell you that?
Yeah, but I didn’t know you did it with Gary. I saw you do it in a class one day at the New School.
Oh, yeah? Yeah. And I did it with this guy a couple days ago, ‘cause I need to do a lot of practice and I get bored playing C major scales so…
How do you do something like that? If, if the… I mean, that would be like telling me that the notes on the piano weren’t where they were supposed to be anymore.
Well, you try to make something out of it, that’s all. You just play it and see what you can make out of it.
And… (laughs) It’s actually fun. It’s not… Oh, but I forgot. What, what was… my train of thought got derailed.
I’m looking at a picture of Jimmy Raney and the (inaudible).
Well, I’ll get you back on the track. Back on the track.
You had just gotten up to the Jimmy Giuffre unusual…
(overlapping/inaudible), which, I think, is fascinating and…
…(then this?) combination, and it was important to you, so I wanted you…
